map:liscor/guild.json:$.entities[2].boar.reason: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted) -- DIEGETIC-DOCUMENT EXCEPTION. A board_rumors 'copy' string is not authorial narration; it is a physical document the player is reading, quoted. Three rules that would otherwise bite are already excepted or satisfied on that basis: (a) section 1.4's two-sentence functional ceiling explicitly excepts 'copy', which is why five sentences is not a breach -- a letter is as long as the letter is; (b) section 8 permits the heading capitals of a 'copy' document, 'whose capitals are the document by definition', and the proxy agrees (caps ['LETTER'], caps_lettering_ctx true); (c) the closing remark sits inside a reported statement attributed to a named in-world speaker -- the Guildmistress's clerk -- so it is a character's aside about the post, not the narrator telling the reader what to think, which is the specific failure the closer ban exists to stop. Flattening it would also cost real content: this letter is the only in-world hook for the Invrisil chain (the hat is Wilovan's signature, and 'the witch at Riverfarm keeps the stones' is the travel affordance), and section 10 guard 1 rules the default action is to leave a string alone.

map:liscor/runners_guild.json:$.entities.reason: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted). Character-bearing register (bible section 3): a present, visible person, observed. 'Not asleep. Not far from it.' is keep-criterion-as-function -- a Gnoll propped against a wall with his legs out reads as asleep, the scene invites exactly that, and whether he is asleep is information the player acts on (he has a talk_pool and a walk-on line, so he can be spoken to). The correction is also the joke and the joke is at nobody's expense. NOTE ON THE COUNTER: extract_prose scores neg_correction 0 on this string -- 'Not asleep.' has no article, so no regex in RE_NEG_CORRECTION matches it. It is nonetheless a negation SEMANTICALLY, and bible section 10 rules that these bind semantically and not lexically. It is therefore counted as runners_guild.json's ONE section 7.3 negation, and per guard 10.2 the keep CONSUMES the file's allowance rather than sitting outside it. That is why the M2a/M2b re-varying of this file's lamp and mud-table strings deliberately introduced no new negation geometry: the restored 'one corner scrubbed, the ridges start again an inch from it' observation is stated positively for exactly this reason, where the string it restores ('One corner is wiped clean and the rest is not.', closer score 3) was both a negation and a button.

Cutting it costs characterisation and buys back only a regex hit. THE EXCEPTION BEING RECORDED: with the sewer grate above, street.json carries TWO negation keeps against section 7.3's per-file ceiling of one. Both are ruled keeps, so the file is knowingly one over. It is bounded and paid for -- this lane cut four negation shapes off the grate alone and removed the cellar door's ('Something was dragged in, and not dragged out.') -- so street.json falls from six-plus shapes to two, and the corpus ceiling of eight (section 7.2) is not threatened by two strings in one file. Recorded here rather than left silent because an unrecorded ceiling breach is indistinguishable from a lane that did not read the rule.

map:liscor/street.json:$.entities[17].ob.reason: GRANTED PETITION (lane-raised, controller-granted), WITH A RECORDED SECTION 3.3 TENSION FOR PHASE 5. Grounds for the keep: one sentence, zero anonymous agents, zero negation, and every element physically present and visible in the scene -- the cart, the absent pin, the man. The wit is compression, not a verdict: the narrator does not tell the reader what the drayman feels or what the scene means, it lists three things and lets the third land. It is also the entry surface for drayman_dispute, whose 'calmed' node is itself a protected keep in protected-keeps.json (the issue's own counterevidence list, 'axle-pin reasoning unfolds messily'). THE TENSION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: bible section 3.3 rules that 'the narrator does not out-perform the character' and is explicitly a read-only principle binding the Phase-5 read and reviewer judgement, not Phase-2 mechanics. This string arguably does out-perform its man -- the drayman's own protected line is deliberately messy and unpolished, and the narrator's introduction of him is neither. The lane's judgement is that the keep is correct and the tension is real, so it is logged here for the Phase 5 cold read to adjudicate with both strings in hand rather than being quietly rewritten now on a principle that was ruled read-only. Counter reading for the record: closer score 1, anon 0, neg 0; 'the whole day over' does NOT trip the section 8 'whole of / the entire' ban (RE_WHOLE requires 'the whole of' or 'the entire').
